contracts: Separate opt-in cache family with no stored credentials, live role or native journal; native document/review session remains the sole source owner.
Source-native save/flush precedes every cache transaction. Exact offline version bytes and publication intents survive failed saves and recovery without recapture.
Local flush and retry are local barriers. Shared flush additionally requires server acceptance and a locally committed receipt for its initially captured queued IDs.
Missing document dependencies remain queued; the catalog never submits ordinary document operations. An optional callback may flush the already-owned document relay.
Frozen complete metadata snapshots cannot roll back an observed immutable prefix. Remote packets are downloaded lazily, natively validated and locally saved before use.
Old principal header semantics remain unchanged. A separate UTF-8 header is supported only by version endpoints; ambiguous/malformed identities refuse.
Delayed packet loading cannot prepare a restore against a changed source or selection. Catalog-only UI updates retain comment drafts/focus; disposal does not close native owners.
remaining: Native suggestions and previews for text, formatting and supported structures; offline decision intents finalized once by authenticated server order with atomic accepted effects.
